territorial_scope.description: Applies to the State of New York and its agencies, political subdivisions and public benefit corporations, and to individuals known or reasonably believed to be located within New York State.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends New York State Finance Law § 165 and § 8 so that the State, its agencies, political subdivisions and public benefit corporations must commission neutral impact assessments and publish use policies before acquiring or using automated decision systems, give notice, provide explanations and human review, and face payment bars and a private right of action. Covers only Sections 7 to 9 of the bill.
summary.long: Sections 7 to 9 of the bill add subdivisions 9 and 10 to State Finance Law § 165 and subdivisions 21 to 25 to State Finance Law § 8. The rules apply to the State and any governmental agency, political subdivision or public benefit corporation of the State that purchases, obtains, uses or accesses information from an automated decision system (ADS). Before doing so, such bodies must engage a neutral third party to conduct an ADS impact assessment and publish it; existing systems are covered within one year of the subdivision's effective date and every two years thereafter, and new systems before acquisition. Use policies must be published at least ninety days before acquisition or deployment of new systems and within 180 days for existing ones. Changes require an addendum, and certain acquisitions or new uses require approval by a city or county council or the state legislature after a public hearing. The Committee on Open Government conducts annual audits; the Office of Information Technology Services must complete a statistical impact study within two years. Bodies must give plain-language notice when an ADS affects decisions, be able to explain decisions, and develop a human review process. Individuals may sue, and the court must award injunctive relief, actual damages or ten thousand dollars per violation (whichever is greater), fees and costs. Section 8 bars payment for such systems unless they use only open source software and the impact assessment and use policy requirements were met, where contracts impair these duties, where they discriminate on enumerated protected factors, or where they make final decisions without human intervention affecting legal rights or deploy or trigger a weapon. The effective date is referenced but not stated in the excerpt.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the text changes scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit or price tier. Day and year periods (ninety days, one hundred eighty days, forty-five days, one year, two years) are procedural time limits and are coded as events. The ten thousand dollar minimum damages per violation in section 165(10)(F)(IV)(B) is a civil remedy amount and is not coded as a threshold.
